subject: Proposed erase window + backup purge alignment for Greenfield Health
messages:
From: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention / purge windows for our pilot environment

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As we start ingesting PHI-adjacent test data for the pilot, our legal team needs a clear picture of your retention and deletion workflows — specifically around backups and log retention. Two asks from our side: 

- Can you provide a concrete backup purge timeline (what gets deleted and when) for tenant data tied to the pilot environment?
- We need to understand any log retention carve-outs (audit/logging for 180 days vs application-level erasure at 30 days).

I've attached a short spreadsheet (Greenfield-retention-summary.xlsx) with current policy expectations. Also, we anticipate a possible short-term legal hold if one of our test subjects triggers an investigation — how would that impact your purge cadence and restore windows?

Please loop in whoever owns retention exceptions and the DPA/subprocessor conversation. We want to finalize the amendment for the pilot by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Maria Ortega
Head of Security
Greenfield Health

---
Attachment: Greenfield-retention-summary.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@greenfieldhealth.com>, Ethan Shaw <procurement@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention / purge windows for our pilot environment

Maria — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Looping Rishi (security/compliance lead) and Marissa (account lead) as you requested.

High level reply so you have something to share with legal today: 
- Application-level data: tenant records are eligible for scheduled erasure 30 days after a deletion request or account termination unless a legal hold is applied.
- Backups / snapshot lifecycle: snapshots are rotated daily and kept for 30 days in hot storage, then moved to cold archive for an additional 60 days before irreversible purge (total 90 days).
- Audit logs: default retention is 180 days (we keep immutable append-only logs for that period).
- Legal holds: a verified legal hold will suspend purge jobs for affected objects across all storage tiers until release; we also provide an escrow restore window of 14 days for live recovery once hold is lifted.

I've attached a proposed one-page schedule (Redwood-proposed-erase-schedule.pdf) that maps the above to concrete dates for a creation on 2027-07-01. Does that align with your expectations?

Open questions for you:
1) Would Greenfield accept a 90-day total snapshot lifecycle for pilot data, or do you require longer retention for backups?
2) For the legal hold scenario, what is the expected SLA for notifying Redwood to trigger a suspension (we can automate a webhook but need a contact point)?

Next steps: if this looks broadly acceptable I'll prep a short MAP and a DPA amendment draft for Marissa and Rishi to review.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

---

Subject: Re: Data retention / purge windows for our pilot environment

Folks — attaching the SOC2 excerpt and a short compliance note. Key confirmations: 

- Snapshot deletion: all snapshots are tagged by tenant_id and deletion jobs accept tenant scoping; audit entries are generated for each purge action (timestamp, actor, snapshot id).
- Restore chain-of-custody: restores create an immutable audit trail and are retained indefinitely in our audit index (searchable by support/legal).
- KMS: keys are customer-segregated (per-tenant CMKs in Dedicated) and KMS admin actions are recorded; for Hosted we offer envelope keys with audit logs retained 365 days on request.

Marissa: will push the SOC2-Snapshot-2026.pdf to the shared Drive link and open OPS-1254 for the implementation tasks (webhook/non-webhook hold flow).

Actionable summary (for Greenfield):
- Pilot default: 90-day snapshot lifecycle + 180-day audit/logs, priced per MAP.
- Optional: 180-day snapshot lifecycle (surcharge).
- Legal hold: signed PDF to security@redwood.com for now; automated webhook implementation tracked under OPS-1254.

I'll hand off to Marissa for MAP and to Alex for the DPA amendment draft.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
